Do you think you're worth 15/hour for working there?

I support raising the minimum wage as do most people who work there. Another interesting question: is it right for CEOs to get paid millions in salaries and then bonuses while many hard working people only make minimum wage? I'm not discussing minimum wage as much as I am asking if you think that your work is worth 15/hour.

I think that the CEO question is simply a logical fallacy. I think that while CEOs should not be making 400/500 times their employees salaries, I also don't believe that working at a fast food restaurant, Starbucks, etc. should equate to $15/hour. I don't think that supporting one means you don't support the other aspect of your point, one can be against both.

I've always thought that the most interesting point of the entire issue is that employees rightfully claim that their salary is no longer a 'living wage' and to me it's clear that the issue is not raising salaries but trying to fix the dollar and inflation which has made life ridiculous. A gallon of gas should not be $4/gallon, nor should milk be 6-7/gallon. Cost of living keeps on skyrocketing and simply fixing the minimum wage devalues other positions at the same time it doesn't fix the real issue of everything else in life skyrocketing.

(Remember when a cellphone was 30/month? Or when college was 2k/semester? Or when you could fill up your tank for 15 bucks? That was in the 90s... really not that long ago.)

Too young to really remember the 90s, but it seems to me that if prices increase than wages should increase as well. $15/hr is still less than many college educated workers can make. How do you see as the best way to fix inflation?

(to be clear I AM for increasing the minimum wage to 10/hour, I think the idea of doubling it is insanity, especially with how it affects entry-level college graduates such as teachers, accountants, and many other positions that start at 30-40k a year)

I think the best way to fix inflation is to fix our government in general. We just wasted how many TRILLIONS of dollars fighting a war in Afghanistan and Iraq? How much money do we spend on supporting military maneuvers in foreign countries in which there is no direct threat to our country? Pork barrel spending out the wazoo? And don't get me started on the new 'fighter jet' that is the biggest scam I've seen yet?

Mix that with how much wasted spending and workarounds people get on taxes? BoA recently was found to have gotten out of billions of dollars in taxable income. That's money that we don't have to shore up our GDP and use towards fixing the dollar. It also means that we have to spend more money taxing other stuff such as gas etc.

Bottom line is I think there are smarter people than me that have written volumes on how to fix the dollar and slow down inflation, but I have gone to college twice in the past 16 years. The first 4 years of that 16 years I spent a total of 12k to go to Purdue University, a well-respected school. Then, 10 years later I finished a second degree from a community college... and am now almost 55k in debt. And that's insanity. 3k/year 16 years ago and now it was 9k/year in 10 years time for a 'lesser' degree. (PU I believe is 12k/semester or year? Don't quote me).

Point being that prices have skyrocketed so I feel the pain, but at the same time I think the major issue is how much inflation is screwing over everyone, while only the rich are able to shelter themselves from the effects. Fixing the issue is not a matter of saying we want a bigger piece of the pie, but more about saying "We need a bigger pie, or a more filling pie".
